cases.reason: Preserve the original passing native proof for options_single_leg_chain_and_quote. Author review for 4.6.70: the new optional budget_conversion argument or BACKTESTING_BUDGET_CONVERSION JSON converts explicitly denominated starting cash using a caller-supplied finite positive rate. Missing provenance and approximate dates remain usable; known later dates are disclosed, not refused. Existing scalar budget/default units, environment amount priority and live broker balances are unchanged. Retained in-memory Pandas option/attention fixtures neither pass a conversion record nor configure its environment variable, so their initialized cash, prices, tool results, decisions, quantities, orders and fills are unchanged. No agent prompt, skill, tool schema or eval fixture changed. Thirteen new native instances failed before implementation; seventeen new instances and two existing live-budget instances passed afterward, covering USD/BTC, a perturbed USDT/USD conversion, ETH/BTC spot, FX, invalid units, optional provenance and legacy/live preservation. Reuse the original actor/judge source, dates, SDK tuple, call identities, timestamps and verdicts; zero new model calls or hosted proof is claimed. The optional settings export also tolerates legacy caller objects without conversion metadata, preserving their existing settings. Its exact pre-fix serialization failure was reproduced natively; that existing check plus four converted and three legacy initialization cases pass after the narrow optional-field read. This affects neither retained fixture cash nor model inputs/decisions and requires no inference replay.
